title: ispace commercial lunar lander
summary: A private Japanese attempt to build a paid lunar delivery service.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

ispace's first lander reached lunar orbit in 2023 but crashed during descent after a software and sensor issue; the company has since rebuilt for further missions with government and commercial payloads. The business model is delivery capacity sold per kilogram, with national space agencies as anchor customers. Landing reliability is the whole product.

Status

Attribute Value
Development stage Proof of concept
Estimated window 2023–2028
Confidence label Speculative
Evidence Editorial synthesis of company, agency and press reporting
Compiled 18 November 2026

Related records

Investment Exposure

Lunar logistics is a reliability business; a single failure can consume years of funding.

What Would Change The View

  • Landing success on the next mission.
  • Signed backlog and cash position.
  • Payload integration partnerships.

Record Notes

Editorial brief, not an imported source note. Named milestones are drawn from company, agency and press reporting; forward dates are announced targets, not verified outcomes. No figure here is an audited statistic.
